title: Kernel membership and independence for products of actual formal representatives
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $\mathcal I$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, and $F=(\mathcal F_r)_{r\geq1}$ a coherent formal module [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Use $B_m=\mathcal I^m/\mathcal I^{m+1}$, $K_0=\mathcal F_1$, $K_n=\ker(\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n)$ for $n>0$, and their projections $\pi_m$ and inclusions $\iota_n$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-kernel-graded-pieces], in sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Fix $m,n\geq0$, an open $U$, actual sections $a\in\mathcal I^m(U)$, $x\in K_n(U)$, and $t\in\mathcal F_{m+n+1}(U)$ whose reduction to $\mathcal F_{n+1}(U)$ is $\iota_n(x)$. Then (1) there is $y\in K_{m+n}(U)$ with $\iota_{m+n}(y)=a t$; and (2) for all $b\in\mathcal I^m(U)$ and $s\in\mathcal F_{m+n+1}(U)$, if $\pi_m(b)=\pi_m(a)$ and the reduction of $s$ is $\iota_n(x)$, then $b s=a t$. No arbitrary quotient sections are lifted and no local sections are glued in this assertion.

source.place: Lemma 087Z (lemma-finite-over-rees-algebra), associated graded construction; Section 0EHN (section-coherent-formal), defining quotient and annihilation conditions. Sources read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087Z and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EHN.

proof.text: Fix a point p, put J = I_p and M = (F_(m+n+1))_p. Use the stalk ideal-product and quotient descriptions. Downward induction identifies (F_(k+1))_p with M/J^(k+1)M for k <= m+n, respecting the reduction maps: the induction step is (M/J^(k+2)M)/J^(k+1)(M/J^(k+2)M) = M/J^(k+1)M since J^(k+2)M is contained in J^(k+1)M. At the top use J^(m+n+1)M = 0, the defining annihilation condition.

If n>0, x belongs to the adjacent kernel, so its image reduces to zero in F_n. The preceding quotient identifications imply t_p belongs to J^n M; for n=0 use J^0 M = M. Thus a_p t_p belongs to J^(m+n)M. If m+n>0 it reduces to zero in the immediately preceding level. Equality can be checked on stalks, so the section a t is in the sectionwise kernel. The sectionwise kernel universal property supplies y. If m+n=0 take y=a t under the identity inclusion.

For representatives b and s satisfying the stated equations, equality of coefficient quotient classes gives b_p-a_p in J^(m+1). Equality of the reductions gives s_p-t_p in J^(n+1)M. Since b_p belongs to J^m and t_p belongs to J^n M, expand b_p s_p-a_p t_p = (b_p-a_p)t_p+b_p(s_p-t_p). Both summands belong to J^(m+n+1)M=0. Stalkwise equality implies equality of the two product sections. On the empty open, sheaf separation supplies equality, and the degree-zero kernel inclusion is the identity.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 087Z (lemma-finite-over-rees-algebra), associated graded construction; Section 0EHN (section-coherent-formal), defining quotient and annihilation conditions. Sources read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/087Z and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EHN. The stalk quotient induction and representative calculation are expanded by Q1.

lean.statement:
theorem formalKernel_representative_product {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : CoherentFormalModule X I) (m n : ℕ) (U : X.Opens)
    (a : (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).1.val.obj (op U))
    (x : (formalKernelPiece F n).val.obj (op U))
    (t : (F.obj.obj (op (m + n))).val.obj (op U))
    (ht : (F.obj.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_left n m)).op).val.app (op U) t =
      (formalKernelι F n).val.app (op U) x) :
    (∃ y : (formalKernelPiece F (m + n)).val.obj (op U),
      (formalKernelι F (m + n)).val.app (op U) y =
        (@id Γ(X, U) ((Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).2.val.app (op U) a)) • t) ∧
    (∀ (b : (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).1.val.obj (op U))
      (s : (F.obj.obj (op (m + n))).val.obj (op U)),
      (formalAssociatedGradedπ I m).val.app (op U) b =
        (formalAssociatedGradedπ I m).val.app (op U) a →
      (F.obj.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_left n m)).op).val.app (op U) s =
        (formalKernelι F n).val.app (op U) x →
      (@id Γ(X, U) ((Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).2.val.app (op U) b)) • s =
        (@id Γ(X, U) ((Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).2.val.app (op U) a)) • t)
